audit.why: TRICKY at 7/10 with a 7.5/10 carry threat matches a 43.18% win rate over 44 games. Left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart is wrong at four positions in both layers. It gives Graves level 1, calls level 2 a skill matchup, hands K'Sante level 3, and gives Graves level 6. The packet chart and every why say K'Sante / Graves / Graves / K'Sante / Skill / K'Sante / K'Sante.
audit.why: whys[0] literally opens 'He out-trades you at Lvl 1'; whys[2] calls level 3 'your strongest window in the lane'; whys[4] calls level 6 an 'Even moment'. Each of those three sits directly under a chart row saying the opposite.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group, with All Out's 120/100/80 and Ntofo Strikes' 3.5s written into the phases so the spikes carry numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors repeated across the page. (a) Smoke Screen is called a blind that makes his autos and Q whiff — it reduces sight range and slows on impact, and it cannot make an ability whiff at all. (b) Graves' Q is called a 'Q-cone' in five places — End of the Line is a single explosive shell with a 1-second fuse that detonates early on terrain; the cone belongs to his R. (c) Collateral Damage is described twice as a wall-escape from his dive — Graves' R does not move him.
audit.why: Each one changes play. Holding W as a defensive blind against Ntofo Strikes is holding it against nothing; aiming a 'cone' as a Q is aiming the wrong shape; and planning to escape All Out with your own ultimate is planning a death.
audit.corrected: W restated as the impact slow plus sight-range cut, which is genuinely useful here because it breaks his step-up; the Q named End of the Line and described as a shell; the fake R-escape removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most exploitable fact about All Out is never mentioned: it transforms K'Sante 'at the cost of reduced defenses', and while All Out his W no longer knocks back or stuns.
audit.why: The page's whole framing is 'fight the tank, never the duelist' — but the duelist form is the one with lower resistances and no hard CC on Path Maker. For a point-blank burst champion that is the window, not the wall. The danger in All Out is his healing and the R knockback that starts it, not his durability.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[6] and spikes[1] as the concrete shape of the level-6 threat: the R knock-through-wall is what kills you, and the reduced-defense body afterwards is what your shells can still hurt.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ntofo Strikes is treated as a poke with no numbers.
audit.why: It is a 3.5-second cooldown and the pull only happens at 2 stacks. That is a countable tell, not a coin flip.

edits.after: Quickdraw online at 16s — weave E in for the point-blank spread and out-DPS him before his stats matter. Two autos and out.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: Full kit at 3: E in, Smoke Screen for the slow, End of the Line point-blank — your best window.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track All Out; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: His HP and resists outpace True Grit, and Path Maker's damage reduction keeps blunting your shells — he reclaims the trades.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Even: Collateral Damage flips a trade, but All Out at 120s answers it — neither side owns level 6.

edits.before: First item spike — the point-blank Q-AA-E-AA pattern now removes half bars. Force fights near walls.
edits.after: His first tank item blunts your burst faster than yours scales into his HP — he edges this spike.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: All Out trades his defenses for damage — that body your shells can still hurt. Otherwise play for picks.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke cuts sight range and slows on impact — drop it on the gank's arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save R as either the execute or the peel knockback. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.
edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage for the slow and sight cut, E through fights for the resists, and save R as the execute. His HP out-lasts you — picks don't care.

edits.before: His duelist mode — fight the tank, never the duelist. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: All Out is 120s and trades his resistances for damage — the knockback that starts it is what kills you.

edits.before: At Lvl 3 your full Q-E-W kit lands: E in, blind his autos and Q with Smoke Screen, dump the Q-cone — your strongest window in the lane.
edits.after: At Lvl 3 your full Q-E-W kit lands: E in, Smoke Screen for the slow and sight cut, then End of the Line point-blank — your strongest window.

edits.before: Even moment: Collateral Damage can flip a trade and wall-escape his dive, but his R all-in answers it, so neither side owns Level 6.
edits.after: Even moment: Collateral Damage can flip a trade he expected to win, but All Out at 120s answers it, so neither side owns Level 6.

edits.before: Your E-in for point-blank shells plus a Q-cone is the only window you out-DPS him before his W damage reduction and HP scaling make your burst tickle. Hold W to blind his auto-and-Q poke.
edits.after: Your E-in for point-blank shells plus End of the Line is the only window you out-DPS him before Path Maker's damage reduction and HP scaling make your burst tickle. Save Smoke Screen's slow for his step-up.

edits.before: Collateral Damage is a real nuke that can win a straight trade, but the instant he hits R he gains a recast knockback, extra range and durability for an all-in, so committing into his ult loses.
edits.after: Collateral Damage is a real nuke, but All Out is a 120-second transform: he knocks you through a wall, dashes after you and heals, and his already 3.5-second Q gets shorter — commit your R only once his is spent.

edits.before: His window: full-build K'Sante's on-hit passive, resists and R (which knocks you through a wall and isolates you) outscale your True Grit stacking and run you down.
edits.after: His window: full-build K'Sante grinds through your shells, and All Out knocks you through a wall and dashes after you — he picks the fight and True Grit doesn't cover the gap.

edits.before: Bait his W charge or Q swipe with a throwaway auto, then dump your real Q-cone and point-blank shells while those cooldowns are down
edits.after: Bait Path Maker's charge or a Q swipe with a throwaway auto, then land End of the Line and your point-blank shells while those are down

edits.before: Hold W to blind him the instant he steps up — it kills his auto-attack and on-hit poke and buys your E-out before his Q can pull you in
edits.after: Drop W on him the instant he steps up — the impact slow and sight cut buy your E-out before two Ntofo Strikes stacks pull you in

edits.before: Soak your Q-cone and shells behind W's damage reduction, then Q-swipe to pull you in and trade his HP against your burst
edits.after: Soak End of the Line and your shells behind Path Maker's damage reduction, then stack Ntofo Strikes twice to pull you in

edits.before: His W (Path Maker) is the whole problem early — it gives him damage reduction while charging and a long knockback, so a clean E-in combo does far less than it would into a squishier bruiser and he can answer your engage. Your one real window is Levels 2-3: weave E for the point-blank shell spread and use your W (Smoke Screen) to blind him so his autos and Q-swipe poke whiff. Bait his W charge or his Q with a single auto before you commit the real Q-cone, because he sustains and reduces what he can't dodge. Take what trades you can here — it only gets worse as his HP climbs.
edits.after: His W (Path Maker) is the whole problem early — damage reduction while charging, then a knockback and stun, so a clean E-in does far less than it would into a squishier bruiser. Your one real window is Levels 2-3: weave E for the point-blank shell spread and drop W (Smoke Screen) on him for the impact slow and the sight cut, which breaks his step-up rather than his damage. Bait the Path Maker charge or a Q with a single auto before you commit End of the Line, because he reduces what he can't dodge. Take what trades you can — it only gets worse as his HP climbs.

edits.before: Through 4-5 he out-stats you — his HP and resists climb faster than your True Grit armor stacking, and his W damage reduction keeps blunting your shell burst. Level 6 is your one even moment: Collateral Damage can flip a trade he expected to win, and you can fire it at a wall to escape his dive. But the second he hits R (All Out) he gains a recast knockback, bonus range and durability and turns the fight into an isolating all-in, so only commit your R when his W and ult are down. Bait the W, blind him with Smoke Screen, then back off — you cannot brawl a 6+ K'Sante straight up.
edits.after: Through 4-5 he out-stats you — his HP and resists climb faster than your True Grit stacks, and Path Maker's damage reduction keeps blunting your shell burst. Level 6 is your one even moment: Collateral Damage can flip a trade he expected to win. But All Out, on 120 seconds at rank 1, knocks you through a wall, dashes after you and heals him, so only commit your R when his W and his ult are down. Bait Path Maker, slow him with Smoke Screen, then back off — you cannot brawl a 6+ K'Sante straight up.

edits.before: This is lost if it goes long. His on-hit passive and tank HP let him grind through your point-blank shells, and his R knocks you through a wall and isolates you from your team, so the True Grit armor and E sustain your kit is built on can't keep you alive in a sustained brawl. Your shells can't out-DPS his durability and W damage reduction, and one R turns a skirmish into a death. Don't try to 1v1 him; group, splitpush the side lane, and use your shell burst to threaten his squishies in fights rather than chipping at his tank body.
edits.after: This is lost if it goes long. His marked-target passive and tank HP let him grind through your point-blank shells, and All Out knocks you through a wall and isolates you from your team, so the True Grit resists your kit is built on can't keep you alive in a sustained brawl. One R turns a skirmish into a death. The one thing in your favour: All Out costs him defenses, so if a fight is already happening his transformed body is the version your shells can still hurt. Don't 1v1 him — group, splitpush, and burst his squishies instead of chipping at him.

notes: The derived flag on K'Sante's W claims trueDamage; Riot's description of Path Maker says nothing about true damage, so I did not assert it anywhere. Same for the flag on Graves' Q ('creates terrain') — his description says the shell detonates on colliding with terrain, not that it makes any. Open judgement call I did not act on beyond stating the fact: the page's slogan is 'fight the tank, never the duelist', but All Out explicitly reduces his defenses and strips the knockback/stun from Path Maker, which for a burst champion argues the opposite. I wrote the mechanic in and left the slogan in dosFull/report untouched rather than reverse the matchup's stated plan on my own judgement.
